title: Declare a deterministic route resolution strategy for every interlocking

facts.note: Hint only: the planner task names interlockings or their route resolution. Broad 'train'/'route' terms alone do not identify the scope; the subject is an interlocking.
Plan artefacts that define train interlockings (the validator's subject_kind is interlocking).
The constraint is validated at CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; every interlocking in the plan is checked then, changed or not. Needs a phase observer.
Detector finding from the coherence/resolved_fact_agreement validator; its presence means a non-compliant interlocking, not mere applicability.

fires: A plan reaches CONFIRM and contains any interlocking, including interlockings unchanged by the current task; each is evaluated (applicability), and only non-compliant ones produce a finding.
A planner authors or edits an interlocking or its routes.
An interlocking has no declared route resolution strategy (non-compliant).
An interlocking declares first_priority but its routes' priorities are duplicated, missing or non-integer (non-compliant).
An interlocking declares fail_on_multiple_match or first_priority with unique integer priorities: the rule still applies and the interlocking is evaluated, and it passes.
doesNotFire: A plan that contains no interlocking subject at all.
Plan edits touching only artefacts that are not interlockings, before CONFIRM validation (e.g. wagon or acceptance wording that does not define an interlocking).

given: A train plan contains an interlocking (whether newly authored, edited, or unchanged)
when: the planner authors or changes it, or the plan is validated at CONFIRM
then: The interlocking must explicitly declare a deterministic route resolution strategy—fail_on_multiple_match, or first_priority with unique integer priorities on its routes—so that ambiguous matching routes fail closed unless resolved by those declared unique priorities.
prefer: Write the strategy name explicitly on the interlocking, using exactly one of the two allowed strategies.
When choosing first_priority, give every route a unique integer priority.
avoid: Leaving the strategy implicit or relying on declaration order or any other undeclared tie-break to pick a route.
Declaring first_priority with duplicate, missing, or non-integer priorities.
Using strategy names other than fail_on_multiple_match and first_priority.
why: Route resolution must be explicit and deterministic; when several routes match, the interlocking must fail closed unless a declared unique priority resolves the ambiguity, rather than picking a route arbitrarily.
evidence: Validator test_sequence_diagram_sanity::test_interlocking_route_resolution_strategy_declared passes at CONFIRM for every interlocking in the plan.
On failure the finding reports interlocking_id, strategy, route_ids, priorities and reason.
verifier_detail: Term route_resolution: allowed strategies are fail_on_multiple_match, or first_priority with unique integer priorities.
Failure evidence fields: interlocking_id, strategy, route_ids, priorities, reason.

trace.note: 'unless unique priority is declared' is kept verbatim in then as the first_priority resolution, not a waiver.
Disposition kept verbatim as 'strict'; no baseline/advisory semantics added.
